elements.element: Renewal is automatic for successive 12-month periods (or only by mutual written agreement)
elements.evidence: "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date"

elements.element: Customer may opt out of / prevent renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by the Company upon thirty (30) days written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Vendor reminder notice 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: "HDI shall notify the Company in writing of each upcoming automatic renewal not less than sixty (60) days prior to the applicable anniversary of the Effective Date."

elements.element: Renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: Clause contains no renewal price-escalation mechanic; the condition is demonstrably absent ("automatically renewed for an additional one year period" with no price uplift), so no cap is required.
"shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period"

elements.element: Customer non-renewal notice window no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "terminated by the Company upon thirty (30) days written notice to HDI" (30 ≤ 60)
No price-increase provision in the clause; conditional requirement inapplicable.

offending_extra_words: Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
reasons: Preferred level is complete on its operative terms: 12-month automatic renewal retained, Customer's non-renewal/termination notice cut to 30 days, and an express 60-day Vendor reminder inserted; no renewal price-escalation mechanic exists in the clause, so the CPI/3% cap condition is absent.
Fallback would also be satisfied (Customer window 30 days ≤ 60; no price increase to cap), but the locked target is preferred and it is met, so no further redline is warranted.

Minimality fails: the replacement span swallowed and re-quoted the untouched sentence "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the \"Termination Date\")." and expanded 32 words to 69 (ratio 2.16). The same result was achievable with a narrow operator/number edit ("by the Company upon thirty (30) days") plus a separate short insertion for the 60-day reminder.
Intent is preserved: HDI's 90-day termination right is expressly retained, the defined term "Termination Date" survives, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Asymmetric notice periods (Company 30 / HDI 90) favour Customer and are consistent with the playbook; the margin comment's offer of a 60-day fallback is non-operative and does not affect the analysis.
